# Harmonic for Hacker News Harmonic for Hacker News is an Android Hacker News client which is meant to be modern, fast and well thought out. You can find it on Google Play for download. This has been my personal side project since 2020 and since starting my PhD in 2021 the time I have to dedicate to Harmonic has decreased. My personal philosophy on side projects is that the most important thing is building something that is actually shipped. Since much of my knowledge on building Android apps is ~10 years old, Harmonic does not use Kotlin or the latest Android API's and is probably not the easiest app to dig into the source code of. However, it is shipped, and it works fairly well in my opinion at least. :) The purpose of open-sourcing Harmonic is thus mainly to enable interested users to submit pull requests fixing issues or adding features. I would like to still be able to find my way around the app's code so I am not looking for a full Kotlin rewrite but if you want to make the app work better with foldables, fix a typo or add support for Android 13's themed icons all that would be much appreciated. I'll still commit things myself when I have time. # Features * Basic account functionality: log in, vote, comment, and submit * Dark theme * Browser choice: integrated or system browser * Key word filtering of stories * Option of "clearing clicked stories" to hide stories you've seen * Ability to export bookmarks to a text file pluginManagement { repositories { google() gradlePluginPortal() } } dependencyResolutionManagement { repositoriesMode.set(RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS) repositories { google() jcenter() maven { url "https://jitpack.io" } } } include ':app' rootProject.name = "Harmonic Hacker News"

steps.message:
Fixed. The build passes (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).

## Root cause

One file: `app/src/main/java/org/sufficientlysecure/htmltextview/LocalLinkMovementMethod.java`.

Comment bodies are `HtmlTextView`s, which install `LocalLinkMovementMethod` as their movement method (`HtmlTextView.java:114`). A long tap on a comment therefore ran **two independent handlers off the same gesture**:

1. `TextView`'s inherited `View.onTouchEvent` detects the long press after ~500 ms and fires the `OnLongClickListener` set in `CommentsRecyclerViewAdapter.ItemViewHolder` (line 428) → the comment menu dialog opens.
2. When the finger lifts, `TextView.onTouchEvent` still forwards the `ACTION_UP` to the movement method, and `LocalLinkMovementMethod` called `link[0].onClick(widget)` **unconditionally** — with no check of how long the press lasted. That reached the adapter's `setOnClickATagListener` → `Utils.openLinkMaybeHN(...)` → the URL opened on top of the dialog.

`View` itself guards against this for normal clicks (it sets `mHasPerformedLongPress` and suppresses the click), but the movement method had no equivalent guard, so the tap-vs-long-tap distinction was simply never made for links.

## The fix

On `ACTION_UP`, the link's `onClick` is skipped when the gesture already qualified as a long press:

```java
if (event.getEventTime() - event.getDownTime() >= ViewConfiguration.getLongPressTimeout())
```

Using the `MotionEvent`'s own `downTime`/`eventTime` keeps the check **stateless**, which matters here because `LocalLinkMovementMethod` is a process-wide singleton (`sInstance`) shared by every `HtmlTextView`; storing the press start in a field would let concurrently-touched views corrupt each other's state. Comparing against the system `getLongPressTimeout()` also means the threshold automatically tracks the user's accessibility setting, staying in sync with whatever `View` used to decide to fire the long click.

Two small robustness additions in the same touch path:
- `ACTION_UP` now clears the pressed-link highlight, which the original code left stuck on after release.
- `ACTION_CANCEL` is handled explicitly, so a link highlighted on `ACTION_DOWN` that then gets taken over by the RecyclerView's scroll no longer stays highlighted.

## Behavior

- Short tap on a URL → opens as before (unchanged).
- Long tap on a URL → comment menu opens, URL does **not** open.
- Long tap elsewhere in a comment, taps on non-link text, and the story-header links (which share this movement method) are all unaffected.

One note: I checked whether the fix belonged in the adapter instead, and the movement method is the right place — the header text in `HeaderViewHolder` routes links through the same class, so both link surfaces are covered by the single change. `UserDialogFragment` uses the platform `LinkMovementMethod`, but it has no long-click listener competing for the gesture, so it has no equivalent bug and needed no change.

2. Long-press handling on comments that opens a comment menu/dialog (e.g. setOnLongClickListener in a comments RecyclerView adapter or ViewHolder).

extra.final_message:
Fixed. The build passes (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).

## Root cause

One file: `app/src/main/java/org/sufficientlysecure/htmltextview/LocalLinkMovementMethod.java`.

Comment bodies are `HtmlTextView`s, which install `LocalLinkMovementMethod` as their movement method (`HtmlTextView.java:114`). A long tap on a comment therefore ran **two independent handlers off the same gesture**:

1. `TextView`'s inherited `View.onTouchEvent` detects the long press after ~500 ms and fires the `OnLongClickListener` set in `CommentsRecyclerViewAdapter.ItemViewHolder` (line 428) → the comment menu dialog opens.
2. When the finger lifts, `TextView.onTouchEvent` still forwards the `ACTION_UP` to the movement method, and `LocalLinkMovementMethod` called `link[0].onClick(widget)` **unconditionally** — with no check of how long the press lasted. That reached the adapter's `setOnClickATagListener` → `Utils.openLinkMaybeHN(...)` → the URL opened on top of the dialog.

`View` itself guards against this for normal clicks (it sets `mHasPerformedLongPress` and suppresses the click), but the movement method had no equivalent guard, so the tap-vs-long-tap distinction was simply never made for links.

## The fix

On `ACTION_UP`, the link's `onClick` is skipped when the gesture already qualified as a long press:

```java
if (event.getEventTime() - event.getDownTime() >= ViewConfiguration.getLongPressTimeout())
```

Using the `MotionEvent`'s own `downTime`/`eventTime` keeps the check **stateless**, which matters here because `LocalLinkMovementMethod` is a process-wide singleton (`sInstance`) shared by every `HtmlTextView`; storing the press start in a field would let concurrently-touched views corrupt each other's state. Comparing against the system `getLongPressTimeout()` also means the threshold automatically tracks the user's accessibility setting, staying in sync with whatever `View` used to decide to fire the long click.

Two small robustness additions in the same touch path:
- `ACTION_UP` now clears the pressed-link highlight, which the original code left stuck on after release.
- `ACTION_CANCEL` is handled explicitly, so a link highlighted on `ACTION_DOWN` that then gets taken over by the RecyclerView's scroll no longer stays highlighted.

## Behavior

- Short tap on a URL → opens as before (unchanged).
- Long tap on a URL → comment menu opens, URL does **not** open.
- Long tap elsewhere in a comment, taps on non-link text, and the story-header links (which share this movement method) are all unaffected.

One note: I checked whether the fix belonged in the adapter instead, and the movement method is the right place — the header text in `HeaderViewHolder` routes links through the same class, so both link surfaces are covered by the single change. `UserDialogFragment` uses the platform `LinkMovementMethod`, but it has no long-click listener competing for the gesture, so it has no equivalent bug and needed no change.
